precepts.text: Into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; sin comes in and wisdom goes out. Ahab was full of sin, so his wisdom was hindered and he had thoughts without understanding, blaming the righteous man for his own doings.
precepts.point: Elijah commanded that all Israel be gathered to Mount Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves that eat at Jezebel's table. Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“For froward thoughts separate from God”. “For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject unto sin.” Sin comes in and wisdom goes out. “For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding, and will not abide when unrighteousness cometh in.”

That is Ahab. He was full of sin, so his wisdom was hindered and he had thoughts without understanding. When he saw Elijah he said, “Art thou he that troubleth Israel?” That is the mind of a wicked person: he blamed the ordained prophet of God for the trouble rather than his own wickedness. When the spirit is gone, wisdom cannot enter a malicious soul.

Elijah answered him with the truth: “I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim.” It was Ahab following the sin of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, worshipping the golden calves, that brought the trouble.

precepts.text: Wisdom exalteth her children and layeth hold of them that seek her; especially with the new, the Most High deals with each differently and gives time to get it right.
precepts.point: Elijah commanded that all Israel be gathered to Mount Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves that eat at Jezebel's table. Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“Wisdom exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seek her.” Those who seek wisdom, she lays hold of and lifts up.

Especially with the new, the Most High deals with each one differently and gives time to get it right. Wisdom is not taken from a man the first time he stumbles. Ahab was not one who sought her; he held on to his sin, followed Baalim, and let Jezebel feed the prophets of Baal and the prophets of the groves at her table without ever checking her.

precepts.text: Wisdom walks with a man by crooked ways at the first, tormenting him in his mind until he rids his body of sin; if he goes wrong she forsakes him and gives him over to his own ruin, which is what happened to Ahab.
precepts.point: Elijah commanded that all Israel be gathered to Mount Carmel with the four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal and the four hundred prophets of the groves that eat at Jezebel's table. Jezebel was the one feeding these eight hundred and fifty false prophets and encouraging them, and Ahab never checked her.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“For at the first she will walk with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread upon him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soul, and try him by her laws.” Wisdom torments a man in his mind at the first, until he rids his body of sin.

“Then will she return the straight way unto him, and comfort him, and shew him her secrets.” That is for the one who comes through the trying.

“But if he go wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruin.” That is what happened to Ahab. He went wrong, wisdom forsook him, and he was given over to his own ruin: blaming Elijah for troubling Israel while he and his father’s house had forsaken the commandments, and letting Jezebel feed eight hundred and fifty false prophets at her table.

precepts.text: Christ said, I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot; I would thou wert cold or hot; so then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spew thee out of my mouth. The lukewarm who know the truth but keep no commandments will be cast away.
precepts.point: Elijah proposed the test: let each side dress a bullock, lay it on wood, and put no fire under, and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. All the people said, It is well spoken.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
Christ said, “I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.”

On Mount Carmel Elijah asked the people, “How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.” That is the lukewarm: one foot in and one foot out, playing the middle ground.

That is a call for all of us to examine ourselves. Cast away every burden and sin, and follow the Most High and his son fully, keeping the commandments. The lukewarm who know the truth but keep no commandments will be cast away. Being spewed out of Christ’s mouth is the end of the middle ground, and the next step after that is death.

precepts.text: I am the Lord, that is my name, and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images. That is why no fire came for Baal.
precepts.point: From midday past the time of the evening sacrifice there was neither voice nor any to answer nor any that regarded. No one answered because the Most High will not give his glory to another, and the gods of the nations are idols that are not real; they are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them the idols cannot answer.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“I am the Lord: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.” That is why no fire came for Baal.

The prophets of Baal dressed their bullock and called on Baal “from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered.” Eight hundred and fifty men leaped upon the altar, running wild, while Elijah sat back watching the madness. At noon he mocked them: “Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.”

They cried aloud and “cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them”, for cutting themselves was part of their false worship whenever they called on Baal. Still “there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.” The Most High will not give his glory to another.

precepts.text: The Lord is great and greatly to be praised, he is to be feared above all gods, for all the gods of the nations are idols, but the Lord made the heavens. The idols of the nations are not real; only the Most High made the heavens.
precepts.point: From midday past the time of the evening sacrifice there was neither voice nor any to answer nor any that regarded. No one answered because the Most High will not give his glory to another, and the gods of the nations are idols that are not real; they are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them the idols cannot answer.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“For the Lord is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.”

The idols of the nations are not real. They are made up by people who have no God, so when they call on them, the idols cannot answer. Only the Most High made the heavens.

That is why, from morning until past the time of the evening sacrifice, with all their crying and cutting, “there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.” There was no one there to answer.

precepts.text: Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture, saith the Lord; the Lord will visit upon them the evil of their doings for feeding his people lies. The same judgment on the prophets of Baal will fall on the false shepherds today.
precepts.point: When all the people saw it they fell on their faces and cried, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God. Elijah commanded, Take the prophets of Baal, let not one of them escape, and they were brought down to the brook Kishon and slain there. In the last days it will be the same: when the Most High rains down fire again by the hands of Christ, no false prophet of Baal will escape, for they that feed the sheep of God lies will not be able to flee.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

precepts.why:
“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” Against the pastors that feed his people he says, “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the Lord.”

When the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the burnt sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the dust, and licked up the water in the trench, the people fell on their faces and said, “The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God.” Then Elijah said, “Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape.” They were brought down to the brook Kishon and slain there.

In the last days it will be the same. When the Most High rains down fire again by the hands of Christ, no false prophet of Baal will escape. They that feed the sheep of God lies will not be able to flee. The same judgment that fell on the prophets of Baal will fall on the false shepherds today; the Lord will visit upon them the evil of their doings.

points: The famine was so sore it was hitting the animals, so Ahab and Obadiah divided the land between them, each going his own way to seek fountains and brooks to find grass to save the horses and mules alive. This was the fruit of the drought Elijah had pronounced.

points: As Obadiah went his way, Elijah met him; Obadiah fell on his face and said, Art thou my lord Elijah? Elijah told him to go tell Ahab that Elijah is here.

points: Obadiah was afraid, for Ahab had searched every nation and kingdom to find and slay Elijah; that is how badly Jezebel wanted him dead, so she got Ahab to do her bidding. This is why Elijah had been on the run, first by Jordan, then years with the widow.

Obadiah feared that the spirit of the Lord would carry Elijah away and Ahab would slay him for a false report, so he pleaded his own record: he feared the Lord from his youth and had hidden a hundred of the Lord's prophets by fifty in a cave. Elijah swore by the Lord of hosts that he would surely show himself to Ahab that day, and so Obadiah went to Ahab, and Ahab came to meet Elijah.
